usedFor: plain number counting — ichi, ni, san, yon/shi…
explanation: Start here for basic Japanese numbers before attaching counters. Includes 1–20 plus 100, 1,000, 10,000, and 100,000.

countTable.note: Both よん and し occur; よん is the safest standalone choice.
Both are common; which reading is preferred depends on context.
きゅう is the usual standalone reading; く appears in some fixed counting contexts.
じゅうよん is the usual neutral choice.

countTable.note: Both occur; context can favor one.

countTable.kana: じゅうきゅう／じゅうく
countTable.note: じゅうきゅう is the usual neutral choice.

notes: 4, 7, and 9 have alternate readings. The natural choice can change when a number is used with a counter, date, time, or fixed expression.
